proposal.utterance: How would you BFO-classify 'the capacity of an institution to repair itself'?

entities.label: InstitutionalSelfRepairCapacity
entities.rationale: A capacity is paradigmatically a Disposition in BFO: it is a specifically dependent continuant that inheres in a bearer (the institution), is internally grounded in the institution's structure and constitution, and is realized when the institution actually undergoes self-repair processes. It is distinguished from a Role (BFO_0000023) because it is grounded in the internal make-up of the bearer rather than in external social relations. It is distinguished from a mere Quality (BFO_0000019) because it is a directedness toward a process (self-repair) that may or may not be triggered. This parallels BFO exemplars like fragility or the capacity to contract.

entities.label: InstitutionalSelfRepairProcess
entities.rationale: The disposition must be realizable in some process. The self-repair of an institution is a Process (BFO_0000015): it unfolds in time, has temporal parts, and constitutes the realization of the InstitutionalSelfRepairCapacity. Minting this class is necessary to fully specify the BFO realization relation and to ground the disposition.

relations.rationale: InstitutionalSelfRepairCapacity is a subclass of Disposition, confirming its BFO typing.

A disposition is realized in a process; the self-repair capacity is realized in instances of InstitutionalSelfRepairProcess. Using BFO_0000054 (realized in) at the class level (as a subclass restriction) captures this directedness.

The capacity for self-repair can be considered a subtype of LegalExistenceCondition insofar as it is among the dispositions that sustain institutional persistence; this is proposed tentatively and flagged for user confirmation.
InstitutionalSelfRepairProcess is a subclass of Process.

open_questions: Should InstitutionalSelfRepairCapacity be typed as a subclass of the existing LegalExistenceCondition (working:LegalExistenceCondition, a Disposition), or should it remain a direct subclass of BFO_0000016 only? The link to LegalExistenceCondition is plausible but not strictly entailed by the utterance.

Is the bearer of this capacity always a LegalInstitution (working:LegalInstitution), or could it also inhere in other kinds of social institutions outside the legal domain? This affects the domain restriction on the inheres-in relation.

Should 'self-repair' be understood narrowly (e.g., constitutional amendment procedures) or broadly (e.g., any adaptive institutional process)? The scope affects whether InstitutionalSelfRepairProcess should be further subdivided.

Is there an intended contrast with InstitutionalPersistence (working:InstitutionalPersistence, a Quality)? If repair is a precondition for persistence, we may want an explicit dependency relation between them.
proposal.rationale_summary: The phrase 'capacity of an institution to repair itself' maps most naturally onto BFO Disposition (BFO_0000016): a specifically dependent continuant that (i) inheres in a bearer (the institution as a material entity), (ii) is grounded in the institution's internal structure rather than in external relational facts (distinguishing it from a Role), and (iii) is directionally oriented toward a specific kind of process—self-repair—which constitutes its realization. Two new classes are proposed: InstitutionalSelfRepairCapacity (Disposition) and InstitutionalSelfRepairProcess (Process), linked by BFO_0000054 (realized in). A tentative subclass link to the existing working:LegalExistenceCondition (also a Disposition) is proposed but flagged as open, since the capacity for self-repair plausibly contributes to institutional existence conditions. No existing classes or individuals in the working ontology are precise enough to reuse without over-generalization.
